**VERDICT: ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS** **Overall Assessment**: The modal implements a structurally sound WAI-ARIA Modal Dialog pattern with robust focus trapping, correct ARIA attribute pairing, and thoughtful backdrop click handling. However, the design contains a synchronous focus-restoration race condition in React's cleanup lifecycle, lacks support for dialog descriptions (`aria-describedby`), and has minor hit-target/forced-colors gaps that degrade real-world assistive technology and touch usability. The core pattern is correct; the reservations are fixable implementation details. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. Focus restoration timing issue in React unmount lifecycle (likely race condition). 2. Missing `aria-describedby` for dialog description per APG Modal Dialog pattern. 3. Close button hit target below WCAG 2.5.8 minimum due to asymmetric padding. 4. Focus indicator may fail in Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode. 5. Backdrop click logic might interfere with screen reader "click" events or miss edge cases. *Actual Findings vs Predictions*: Predictions 1-4 materialized as findings. Prediction 5 did not manifest; the `mousedown` + `click` guard is safe for AT because the overlay is non-focusable and uses `role="presentation"`. The focus trap itself was stronger than predicted, correctly handling dynamic DOM changes and out-of-bounds focus. --- **Critical Findings** (blocks access): *None. The component does not block core functionality for any user group.* **Major Findings** (significantly degrades experience): 1. **Synchronous focus restoration on unmount risks focus loss in React 18+** - **Evidence**: `Modal.tsx:48-50` cleanup function calls `previouslyFocusedElement.current?.focus()` synchronously during component teardown. - **User Group**: Keyboard & Screen Reader users - **WCAG/APG**: WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern (Focus Management), WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap - **Expected**: Focus returns reliably to the trigger element after modal closes, regardless of React rendering mode or concurrent updates. - **Actual**: In React 18+ with concurrent features or rapid state updates, synchronous cleanup focus assignment can be dropped before the DOM settles, leaving focus on `` or the last tabbable element inside the unmounting dialog. - **Fix**: Defer focus restoration: `setTimeout(() => previouslyFocusedElement.current?.focus(), 0);` or use a callback ref on the trigger button passed via props. Add a fallback check: `if (document.activeElement === modalRef.current) { ... }`. 2. **Missing `aria-describedby` support for dialog description** - **Evidence**: `Modal.tsx:136-137` dialog element lacks `aria-describedby`; children are rendered directly into `.modal-body` without an associated description region. - **User Group**: Screen reader users navigating complex dialogs (forms, multi-step wizards, long instructions) - **WCAG/APG**: WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern (Description), WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - **Expected**: Long-form dialog content should be programmatically associated with the dialog via `aria-describedby` so AT announces context before reading content. - **Actual**: Screen readers only announce the title (`aria-labelledby`). Users must tab into the dialog to discover its purpose or instructions. - **Fix**: Add an optional `description` prop. Render `
{description}
` and apply `aria-describedby="modal-desc"` to the dialog when provided. **Minor Findings** (friction but workaround exists): 1. **Close button hit target height below WCAG 2.5.8 minimum** - **Evidence**: CSS `.modal-close` uses `padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 24px;`. Computed height ≈ 32px, width ≈ 16px. - **User Group**: Touch users, motor impairment users - **WCAG/APG**: WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) - **Expected**: Interactive targets ≥ 24×24 CSS pixels (or 44×44 recommended). - **Actual**: Width is too narrow for reliable touch/cursor targeting. - **Fix**: Add `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px;` or adjust padding to `8px 12px`. 2. **Focus indicator may be overridden in forced-colors mode** - **Evidence**: CSS `.modal-dialog:focus { outline: 3px solid #0066cc; }` and `.modal-close:focus { outline: 2px solid #0066cc; }` - **User Group**: Low vision users on Windows High Contrast / macOS High Contrast - **WCAG/APG**: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance - **Expected**: Focus indicators must remain visible and distinct in forced-colors mode. - **Actual**: User agents often strip custom `outline` colors in forced-colors, reverting to system defaults or removing them entirely if not explicitly preserved. - **Fix**: Add `@media (forced-colors: active) { .modal-dialog:focus, .modal-close:focus { outline: 2px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 1px; } }` **Enhancements** (best practice not met): - Provide a `role="alertdialog"` variant or prop for critical warnings. APG recommends `alertdialog` when immediate user acknowledgment is required, as it changes focus behavior and announcement urgency. - Consider adding `role="document"` to `.modal-body` if the dialog contains multiple paragraphs or complex content. APG suggests this improves screen reader navigation within large dialogs. **What's Missing** (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions): - **Dynamic focusable state handling**: While the trap recomputes on every `Tab`, elements that become `disabled` or `hidden` *after* initial render are correctly skipped by `getClientRects().length > 0`. However, if a child uses `aria-disabled="true"` (common in React), it won't be filtered out. Add `!el.hasAttribute('aria-disabled')` to the filter. - **Missing `inert` fallback**: `aria-modal="true"` handles background inertness for AT, but modern browsers support the `inert` attribute natively. Adding `inert` to the overlay or background container improves keyboard isolation in older AT and non-standard UAs. - **No loading/error state hooks**: The component is a structural container. Consumers must manage `aria-busy`, `aria-live`, or error associations themselves. Document this expectation in props/comments. **Multi-Perspective Notes**: | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | MEDIUM | Missing `aria-describedby` for complex dialogs; synchronous focus restore risk | | Keyboard-only | LOW | Focus trap is complete and robust; escape key handled correctly | | Low vision | MEDIUM | Hit target width too narrow; focus indicator may fail in forced-colors | | Cognitive | LOW | Clear title, predictable close behavior, no timeouts or complex interactions | | Vestibular & motion | LOW | No animations/transitions defined | | Auditory access | LOW | N/A (no media) | | Environmental contrast | MEDIUM | Custom focus colors may not survive UA forced-colors overrides | **Verdict Justification**: The modal implements the core WAI-ARIA Modal Dialog pattern correctly: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` pairing, robust focus trapping with dynamic DOM recomputation, and proper escape key handling. The backdrop click logic is well-scoped and safe for AT. Realist Check on severity: - Focus restoration race condition (MAJOR): Downgraded from CRITICAL because synchronous cleanup works in standard React 17/18 sync rendering, but remains a documented anti-pattern for concurrent features. Mitigated by `setTimeout(0)` or callback ref. - Missing `aria-describedby` (MAJOR): Real impact only when dialogs contain instructions/forms >2 paragraphs. Mitigated by making it optional via props. - Hit target & forced-colors (MINOR): Low user impact in desktop mouse usage; higher impact on touch/contrast modes. Straightforward CSS fixes. The design is coherent and defensible. Upgrading to ACCEPT requires: (1) deferring focus restoration, (2) adding `aria-describedby` support, (3) fixing hit target/forced-colors CSS, and (4) filtering `aria-disabled` in the focusable selector. **Open Questions (unscored)**: - Does the consuming application use React 18+ concurrent features or strict mode? If yes, the focus restoration race condition becomes HIGH confidence. - Will this modal ever contain long-form instructions or multi-step forms? If yes, `aria-describedby` support is mandatory, not optional. - Are there any parent components that programmatically disable children while the modal is open? If so, verify `aria-disabled` filtering works as expected in your runtime.
